data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003's claim that distinguishing evidence is found in the 'joint distribution of failure' is undercut by its own analogy. The analogy's shared structure states that 'shared history creates a memory that causes the system to fail when the input changes, even if the components are independent.' If components fail due to a shared memory/history, their failures are definitionally NOT independent — yet the target labels the components as independent. This internal contradiction means the proposed evidence (joint distribution of failure) cannot distinguish truly independent failures from shared-history failures, because the target has already conceded that shared-history failures occur in components it calls independent. The evidence criterion collapses the very distinction it is supposed to draw.
